Since the deformation traces of the deep structural layers of the lithosphere can be exposed under tectonic action, in some special structural parts, the structural traces formed by different structural layers of the lithosphere during the same tectonic process can "co-exist". A detailed structural analysis of such structural sites, supplemented by analysis of petrology, geochemistry and chronology, can gain new understanding. For example, based on the observation of low-angle normal faults in the North American Cordillera, Wernicke[1] and Lister et al.[2] proposed that low-angle normal faults are ductile shear zones in the middle crust, formed by extensional detachment (Fig. 2), the footwall formed a metamorphic core complex and the hanging wall formed a basin and range structure due to tilting. On the profile, the metamorphic core complex is composed of deep core metamorphic complex, middle-level ductile shear-detachment fault and shallow-level brittle deformation structure, and has the characteristics of three-layer structure. For an in-depth analysis of ductile detachment faults, the type of shear action and its variation can be quantitatively determined by kinematic vorticity, so as to establish a structural kinematic model[7, 9]. In the Hunan-Hubei-Chongqing-Sichuan border area of the middle and upper Yangtze in South China, Yan et al. [10], through the observation and analysis of the relationship between different styles of fault-fold combinations under the condition of thrust and nappe, proposed that the shallow lithosphere structure consists of multiple The thick-skinned-thin-skinned structural model of layered progressive pushover controlled by layer detachment structure (Fig. 3). The above shows that multi-layer detachment tectonics can develop in different structural layers of lithosphere. Fig. 2. 	Three delaminated tectonic models in the formation of low-angle normal faults and metamorphic core complex structures[1,2] Brittle upper crust; 2. Ductile crust; 3. Lithospheric upper mantle; 4. Asthenosphere; 5. Magmatic rock② Evidence from deep geophysical exploration. The most important evidence support for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere comes from the results of deep geophysical exploration, including deep seismic reflection, magnetotelluric sounding, and Bouguer gravity anomaly detection. After the 5.12 Longmenshan Wenchuan Earthquake in 2008, Burchfiel et al. [11], based on data such as the Bouguer gravity anomaly, believed that the upper crust of Longmenshan did not thicken significantly, but the middle and lower crust with one to several layers of ductile flow crust was flowing eastward. In the process, it was blocked and thickened by the hard central Sichuan block under the Sichuan Basin, resulting in the vertical uplift of Longmenshan and the accumulation of abnormal stress, which eventually led to the Wenchuan earthquake in May 2008. This indicates that there is a multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere in the Longmen Mountains and the area to the west. This structural model of Burchfiel et al. [11] further proves that the passage (or channel) flow mode [5~7]. In many mountain ranges, detachment faults have been recognized as one of the dominant factors of orogeny, such as the use of deep reflection seismic profiling (CORCOP) to discover a huge near-horizontal fault beneath the Blue Ridge of the Appalachians in the United States Thrust detachment zone, and pushed the Precambrian crystalline rock series of the Blue Ridge on the sedimentary cover of the Lower Paleozoic, and the thrust distance from the southeast to the northwest of the 5-15km thick foreign rock sheet Up to 260km[3, 4]. ③ Supported by experimental simulation results. In order to verify the multi-layer detachment structure model of the lithosphere, people use petrological and geochemical analysis methods, or carry out relevant high-temperature, high-pressure and petrological experimental analysis on rock samples at different structural levels, and on this basis put forward The delamination structural model of the lithosphere [12] better explains the deep structural detachment of the lithosphere. Figure 3 	Formation model of multi-layered detached nappe thin-skinned structures in the South China Yangtze block [6] Fz, Fc, Fs and Ft represent the structural detachment of the Sinian base, Cambrian base, Silurian and Triassic lower parts, respectively Some key scientific issues involved in the detachment surface[10] Although the multi-layer detachment structural model of the continental lithosphere has been supported by some observations and experimental evidence, there are still some key scientific issues that have not been resolved. Therefore, the multi-layer detachment structural model It is still a working hypothesis. These scientific issues mainly include: ① How to determine the interface properties of structural layer detachment? That is, what is the underground originality? For example, the physical properties and deformation behavior of the structural layer interface are the most critical issues in the deformation of multi-layer detachment structures. What we have observed in the field is the structural traces of the lithosphere exposed to the surface after multi-layer detachment and deformation. However, the interface inferred from deep geophysical data has multiple solutions. How to compare it with surface observations becomes a solution. the crux of the matter. Some researchers have also proposed to use high temperature and high pressure experiments to test. However, due to the limitation of the strain rate and boundary conditions such as temperature and pressure during the experiment, the current simulation is far from the actual environment of natural deformation. ② What is the deformation process of structural layer detachment? That is, what kind of deformation and metamorphism process has it experienced? When we observe on the surface, we invert the deformation process according to some structural kinematics pointing signs during the deformation. However, during the observation process, it was also found that many kinematic directions at the same time were inconsistent or even opposite. In addition, the deformation process we are inverting now does not limit the time and deformation rate, and even completely ignores the deformation process. Therefore, this inversion process may be very different from the natural process. ③ Reasons for deformation differences between structural layers? Among the different structural layers observed in the field, there are huge differences in deformation structural styles and combinations, as well as the metamorphic temperature-pressure conditions reflected by them, but the interface between the two layers, that is, the ductile detachment shear zone, may sometimes only be a few centimeters. What is the reason, what is the tectonic process, and the tectonic force can cause such a huge deformation-metamorphism difference between the upper and lower structural layers? ④ How big is the scale of delamination? Since the multi-layer detachment is based on the observation of low-angle faults, the change and extension scale/depth of low-angle faults are the most important basis for determining the scale of delamination. However, there is no research example so far that can accurately determine The occurrence change and scale of low-angle faults to the deep. Another question related to this is whether this kind of delamination structure only occurs in the middle and upper part of the lithosphere, or can it occur in the entire continental lithosphere? For example, is the delamination at the bottom of the lithosphere[12] a type of delamination tectonics? ⑤ Is there really a middle and lower crustal ductile channel flow in the middle and lower crust? Is it one layer or several layers? Is the multilayer detachment tectonics of the lithosphere controlled by the flow of these ductile flow shells? Or to what extent can the ductile flow crust control the deformation of the lithosphere? How to determine the nature of this fluid? There are no definitive answers to questions about the relative viscosities or rheology of fluids. Since the above key problems have not been resolved, traditional structural geology field observations are limited by surface rock outcrops, there are uncertainties and multi-solutions in the interpretation of deep geophysical detection data, and rock geochemical data have limitations in geological relationship analysis. Insufficient, especially the boundary conditions set by experimental structural geology are far from satisfying the physical, chemical and geological reality of the deep deformation of the continental lithosphere. Therefore, only by combining the studies of structural geology, geophysics and rock geochemistry, and realizing the complementary advantages of multiple disciplines, can objectively carry out more in-depth research on the multi-layer delamination structure of the lithosphere. With the continuous refinement of field structural analysis and the discovery of new important evidence and key structural phenomena, coupled with the continuous application of modern testing and simulation techniques in the field of earth sciences, the temperature-pressure conditions at different depths of the lithosphere and their Morphing features will gradually become a reality. On the basis of these studies, the continental lithosphere multi-layer delamination model will be continuously revised and improved.

question: A GIS workload uses eight equal-sized memory pages: continental shelf, continental slope, continental base, and N1–N5, each explicitly outside the continental margin. Each of 3,000 annual accesses selects the continental-margin class with probability 0.8 or the nonmargin class with probability 0.2, then selects a page uniformly within that class. Residency is fixed for the year. Plan A keeps only the shelf resident for an annual fee of 0 yuan; Plan B keeps all continental-margin pages resident for 300 yuan; Plan C keeps only the shelf and slope resident for 100 yuan. Each nonresident access causes one page fault costing 1 yuan; resident accesses cost nothing beyond the annual fee. Which conclusion correctly selects the minimum expected annual budget and characterizes the locality underlying virtual storage management? Tuples below are ordered by Plans A, B, C.

options.A: Choose Plan C: expected annual budgets are (1,800, 900, 700) yuan. Locality is uneven page-access frequency.
options.B: Choose Plan A: expected annual fault counts are (2,200, 600, 1,400), and the compared costs are fixed fees (0, 300, 100) yuan. Locality is uneven page-access frequency.
options.C: Choose Plan B: expected annual budgets are (2,200, 900, 1,500) yuan. Locality is uneven page-access frequency.
options.D: Choose Plan A: expected annual budgets are (800, 2,700, 1,700) yuan. Locality makes greater residency of frequently accessed pages increase fault costs.

explanation: The continental margin includes the shelf, slope, and base. Each margin page therefore has access probability 0.8/3 = 4/15, while each nonmargin page has probability 0.2/5 = 1/25. This uneven distribution of memory accesses illustrates locality; geographic proximity alone is not the relevant principle. Conditional on a margin access, fault probabilities for Plans A, B, C are 2/3, 0, and 1/3. Conditional on a nonmargin access, all three fault probabilities are 1. By the law of total probability, overall fault probabilities are 11/15, 1/5, and 7/15, giving expected annual fault counts of 2,200, 600, and 1,400. Adding fixed fees to expected faults times 1 yuan gives annual budgets of 2,200, 900, and 1,500 yuan. Plan B is cheapest.

distractor_analysis.reason: It excludes the continental base from the margin, incorrectly using two margin pages and six nonmargin pages. Under that misclassification, the calculated budgets become 1,800, 900, and 700 yuan, but the base belongs to the margin.

It correctly calculates expected faults and identifies locality, but compares fixed fees alone rather than integrating fault costs into the annual budgets. The lowest fixed fee does not imply the lowest total budget.

It reverses the residency–fault relationship, using resident-access probabilities 4/15, 4/5, and 8/15 as fault probabilities. This produces the stated budgets, but resident accesses cause no faults; covering frequently accessed pages reduces fault costs.

question:
Among the four necessary conditions for deadlock, the one that cannot be broken is the mutual exclusion of resources.
Respond with True or False.
answer:

question_plan: Ask for an integrated audit of a hypothetical hospital scheduler whose indivisible operating-room resources require mutual exclusion. Compare three proposed responses to resource deadlock: allow simultaneous use of an exclusive resource; change a consented debridement into an expressly refused, nonemergency amputation to simplify scheduling; or preserve consent and exclusivity while imposing one global resource-acquisition order before procedures begin. Ask which response is acceptable and which deadlock condition it targets. For auditing the existing workflow, define A as a report of nonemergency surgery beyond explicit consent during a resource-allocation incident. Supply two exhaustive, disjoint workflow strata with hypothetical probabilities 0.30 and 0.70 and conditional A rates 0.20 and 0.05. Ask what proportion of all incidents should be flagged as A and routed to a health-related legal-complaint queue, explaining why this routing does not itself establish malpractice.

answer_plans.plan: Choose globally ordered acquisition of exclusive resources before procedures begin, breaking circular wait while retaining the source sample's unbreakable mutual-exclusion condition for these resources. Reject replacing consented debridement with expressly refused nonemergency amputation: scheduling convenience does not overcome the patient's refusal. Treat reports of that conduct as medical-setting rights complaints within the health-related legal category, without asserting that classification proves liability. Apply the law of total probability to obtain P(A)=0.30(0.20)+0.70(0.05)=0.095, so 9.5% of incidents are flagged for this rights-related review.

Preserve mutual exclusion, recommend globally ordered acquisition, correctly calculate the 9.5% report rate, and recognize that patient-rights complaints belong in the health-related legal queue. Nevertheless, accept the nonemergency amputation substitution as an operationally useful option, omitting the significance of the patient's express refusal and limited consent.

State separately that mutual exclusion must remain, refused nonemergency amputation is inappropriate, patient-rights complaints are health-related, and the law of total probability gives 9.5%. Do not use these facts to select a scheduler policy, identify the condition that policy breaks, or connect the computed rate to the specified review queue.

Correctly reject surgery beyond consent, classify the reports as health-related, and calculate 9.5%, but argue that the need to protect patient rights authorizes simultaneous allocation of an indivisible resource. Incorrectly claim that removing mutual exclusion is the appropriate deadlock remedy rather than preserving it and breaking circular wait.

medical.necessity: Establishes the limited procedure the patient authorized, against which the proposed scheduling substitution must be assessed.
Makes the proposed amputation contrary to the patient's stated wishes rather than merely an unspecified treatment choice.
Supports rejecting the override in the stipulated nonemergency setting and defining the incidents requiring rights review.

legal.necessity: Connects surgery beyond explicit consent to the rights-related scope of the legal intake category.
Determines the appropriate intake queue for the incident reports counted by the probability calculation.
The affirmative classification of an allegation supports routing a complaint without treating its assertions as an established malpractice finding.

mathematics.necessity: Ensures that the two workflow strata cover all incidents without double-counting.
Provides the stratum-specific rates of reports meeting the consent-override definition.
Combines the conditional rates with stratum frequencies to obtain the overall 9.5% flagging rate.

True Religion Apparel, Inc., together with its subsidiaries and affiliates (collectively, the “Company”), is dedicated to upholding fair and legal employment practices and environmental sustainability requirements.

As an integral component of this commitment, we have developed and implemented an Associate Code of Conduct (the “Code,” available here), which applies to all vendors, manufacturers, contractors, and suppliers (“Associates”) that form a part of our supply chain.

The Code advises our Associates of their obligation to adhere to all applicable local, state (including the California Transparency in Supply Chain Act) and federal laws as well as the standards established by the Company and set forth in the Code.

The core elements of our Code are prohibitions on discrimination, forced labor, and child labor, insistence on fair wages and hours and the provision of safe and healthy working conditions, as well as guidelines for minimizing each Associate’s environmental footprint.

As a condition of doing business with the Company, each Associate must execute the Code and implement the principles contained therein.

The Company will continue to develop Associate monitoring systems including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced third party audits to assess and ensure compliance with the Code.

If the Company determines that any Associate has violated the Code, the Company may either terminate its business relationship or require the Associate to implement a corrective action plan.

The Act, which became effective January 1, 2012, requires certain retail sellers and manufacturers to disclose their efforts to eradicate slavery and human trafficking from their direct supply chains. It is intended to provide consumers with the means to determine which companies have an active social responsibility program and thereafter to make conscientious purchasing decisions.

(2) Audits

The Company relies on independent third party vendors to conducts unannounced audits of Associates, which assist in the evaluation of Associates’ compliance with Company’s supply chain standards for trafficking and slavery.

(3) Integrity of Components

By executing the Code, every Associate certifies that materials incorporated into goods and merchandise manufactured for the Company comply with labor and trafficking laws, and with all other applicable laws, rules and regulations of the respective country or countries in which they do business.

(4) Accountability

Associates must manifest their commitment to the implementation of the Code’s stated anti-slavery and human trafficking principles by maintaining or establishing an appropriate management system (with adequate documentation and record-keeping in place) to address compliance with these principles and detection and correction of any non-compliance.

(5) Training

In connection with its commitment to enforce and uphold the principles set forth in the Code, the Company provides training on recognizing the warning signs of human trafficking and slavery to those employees who have direct responsibility for supply chain management.

It is intended to provide consumers with the means to determine which companies have an active social responsibility program and thereafter to make conscientious purchasing decisions.

(3) Integrity of Components

By executing the Code, every Associate certifies that materials incorporated into goods and merchandise manufactured for the Company comply with labor and trafficking laws, and with all other applicable laws, rules and regulations of the respective country or countries in which they do business.

Associates must manifest their commitment to the implementation of the Code’s stated anti-slavery and human trafficking principles by maintaining or establishing an appropriate management system (with adequate documentation and record-keeping in place) to address compliance with these principles and detection and correction of any non-compliance.

(5) Training

question: A hospital scheduler uses indivisible operating-room resources that require mutual exclusion. Three deadlock responses are proposed: (I) allow simultaneous use of an exclusive resource; (II) replace consented debridement with an expressly refused, nonemergency amputation to simplify scheduling; (III) preserve consent and exclusivity and require all procedures to acquire resources in the same global order, established before procedures begin. For an audit of the existing workflow, let A mean a report of nonemergency surgery beyond explicit consent during a resource-allocation incident. Two exhaustive, disjoint workflow strata contain 30% and 70% of incidents, with conditional A rates of 20% and 5%, respectively. Which audit conclusion correctly selects the acceptable response, identifies the deadlock condition it targets, and determines the proportion to flag and route for health-related legal review?

options.A: Accept II and III; III breaks circular wait. Route 9.5% of incidents to health-related legal review, without a malpractice finding.
options.B: Accept III only; it breaks circular wait. Route 9.5% of incidents to health-related legal review, without a malpractice finding.
options.C: Retain exclusivity and reject refused amputation; patient-rights complaints are health-related and P(A) is 9.5%. Leave scheduler selection, the targeted condition, and routing undecided.
options.D: Accept I only as a patient-rights safeguard; it breaks mutual exclusion. Route 9.5% of incidents to health-related legal review, without a malpractice finding.

explanation: These indivisible resources require mutual exclusion, so simultaneous use is not a valid remedy. A common global acquisition order prevents circular wait while preserving exclusivity. Debridement-only consent and express refusal rule out substituting a nonemergency amputation for scheduling convenience. By the law of total probability, P(A) = 0.30 × 0.20 + 0.70 × 0.05 = 0.095. Thus, 9.5% of incidents should be flagged for health-related legal review as reports concerning rights in a medical setting. Intake classification identifies the subject of a complaint; it does not verify the allegation or establish malpractice.

distractor_analysis.reason: It correctly identifies ordered acquisition, circular wait, the report rate, and the review queue, but accepts an expressly refused nonemergency amputation despite consent being limited to debridement.

It lists correct facts from the participating domains without integrating them into the requested audit decision: selecting III, identifying circular wait, and routing the calculated share to the specified queue.

It incorrectly treats protection of patient rights as permission to share a resource that requires exclusive use. Rights protection does not remove that resource constraint; the acceptable remedy preserves mutual exclusion and breaks circular wait.

question_plan: Ask for an integrated audit of a hypothetical hospital scheduler whose indivisible operating-room resources require mutual exclusion. Ask which response is acceptable and which deadlock condition it targets. For auditing the existing workflow, define A as a report of nonemergency surgery beyond explicit consent during a resource-allocation incident. Supply two exhaustive, disjoint workflow strata with hypothetical probabilities 0.30 and 0.70 and conditional A rates 0.20 and 0.05. Ask what proportion of all incidents should be flagged as A and routed to a health-related legal-complaint queue, explaining why this routing does not itself establish malpractice.

answer_plans.plan: Choose globally ordered acquisition of exclusive resources before procedures begin, breaking circular wait while retaining the source sample's unbreakable mutual-exclusion condition for these resources. Reject replacing consented debridement with expressly refused nonemergency amputation: scheduling convenience does not overcome the patient's refusal. Treat reports of that conduct as medical-setting rights complaints within the health-related legal category, without asserting that classification proves liability. Apply the law of total probability to obtain P(A)=0.30(0.20)+0.70(0.05)=0.095, so 9.5% of incidents are flagged for this rights-related review.

Preserve mutual exclusion, recommend globally ordered acquisition, correctly calculate the 9.5% report rate, and recognize that patient-rights complaints belong in the health-related legal queue. Nevertheless, accept the nonemergency amputation substitution as an operationally useful option, omitting the significance of the patient's express refusal and limited consent.

State separately that mutual exclusion must remain, refused nonemergency amputation is inappropriate, patient-rights complaints are health-related, and the law of total probability gives 9.5%. Do not use these facts to select a scheduler policy, identify the condition that policy breaks, or connect the computed rate to the specified review queue.

Correctly reject surgery beyond consent, classify the reports as health-related, and calculate 9.5%, but argue that the need to protect patient rights authorizes simultaneous allocation of an indivisible resource. Incorrectly claim that removing mutual exclusion is the appropriate deadlock remedy rather than preserving it and breaking circular wait.

legal.necessity: Connects surgery beyond explicit consent to the rights-related scope of the legal intake category.

The affirmative classification of an allegation supports routing a complaint without treating its assertions as an established malpractice finding.

True Religion Apparel, Inc. Corporate Responsibility



True Religion Apparel, Inc., together with its subsidiaries and affiliates (collectively, the “Company”), is dedicated to upholding fair and legal employment practices and environmental sustainability requirements.

As an integral component of this commitment, we have developed and implemented an Associate Code of Conduct (the “Code,” available here), which applies to all vendors, manufacturers, contractors, and suppliers (“Associates”) that form a part of our supply chain.

The Code advises our Associates of their obligation to adhere to all applicable local, state (including the California Transparency in Supply Chain Act) and federal laws as well as the standards established by the Company and set forth in the Code.

The core elements of our Code are prohibitions on discrimination, forced labor, and child labor, insistence on fair wages and hours and the provision of safe and healthy working conditions, as well as guidelines for minimizing each Associate’s environmental footprint.

As a condition of doing business with the Company, each Associate must execute the Code and implement the principles contained therein.

The Company will continue to develop Associate monitoring systems including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced third party audits to assess and ensure compliance with the Code.

If the Company determines that any Associate has violated the Code, the Company may either terminate its business relationship or require the Associate to implement a corrective action plan.

By espousing the foregoing principles, the Company strives to ensure integrity of its supply chain while continuing to uphold and exceed the quality of our branded merchandise.



2012 California Transparency in Supply Chain Act (SB 657) (the “Act”)

The Act, which became effective January 1, 2012, requires certain retail sellers and manufacturers to disclose their efforts to eradicate slavery and human trafficking from their direct supply chains. It is intended to provide consumers with the means to determine which companies have an active social responsibility program and thereafter to make conscientious purchasing decisions.

The points outlined below highlight the Act’s mandatory disclosures, followed by an explanation of how the Company is addressing each of them:

(1) Verification

The Company continues to develop monitoring systems to assess and ensure Associate’s compliance with the slavery and human trafficking prohibitions set forth in the Code through various means, including, but not limited to, independent, unannounced on-site third party verification visits.

(2) Audits

The Company relies on independent third party vendors to conducts unannounced audits of Associates, which assist in the evaluation of Associates’ compliance with Company’s supply chain standards for trafficking and slavery.

(3) Integrity of Components

By executing the Code, every Associate certifies that materials incorporated into goods and merchandise manufactured for the Company comply with labor and trafficking laws, and with all other applicable laws, rules and regulations of the respective country or countries in which they do business.

(4) Accountability

Associates must manifest their commitment to the implementation of the Code’s stated anti-slavery and human trafficking principles by maintaining or establishing an appropriate management system (with adequate documentation and record-keeping in place) to address compliance with these principles and detection and correction of any non-compliance.

(5) Training

In connection with its commitment to enforce and uphold the principles set forth in the Code, the Company provides training on recognizing the warning signs of human trafficking and slavery to those employees who have direct responsibility for supply chain management.

question: A hospital scheduler allocates indivisible operating-room resources that require mutual exclusion. Three deadlock responses are proposed: I, allow simultaneous use of an exclusive resource; II, replace consented debridement with an expressly refused, nonemergency amputation to simplify scheduling; III, preserve consent and exclusivity and require resource acquisition in one global order before procedures begin. For auditing existing resource-allocation incidents, let A denote a report of nonemergency surgery beyond explicit consent. Two exhaustive, disjoint workflow strata contain 30% and 70% of incidents, with conditional A rates of 20% and 5%, respectively. A health-related legal-complaint queue covers alleged care failures and medical-setting rights complaints. Which complete audit correctly selects the acceptable response, identifies its deadlock target, and determines the proportion of all incidents to route as A without treating routing as proof of malpractice?

options.A: Accept II and III; III breaks circular wait while preserving exclusivity. Route 9.5% to the health-related legal queue for review, not as proven malpractice.
options.B: Preserve exclusivity and reject II. The overall A rate is 9.5%, and medical-rights complaints are health-related; leave scheduler policy, deadlock target, and routing unspecified.
options.C: Accept III only; it breaks circular wait while preserving exclusivity and consent. Route 9.5% to the health-related legal queue for review, not as proven malpractice.
options.D: Accept I only and reject II; protecting patient rights justifies breaking mutual exclusion through simultaneous allocation. Route 9.5% to the health-related legal queue for review, not as proven malpractice.

explanation: Mutual exclusion cannot be removed for the stipulated indivisible resources. Requiring acquisitions to follow one global order prevents circular wait without permitting simultaneous use. Scheduling convenience also cannot justify an expressly refused, nonemergency amputation when consent covers only debridement. By the law of total probability, P(A) = 0.30 × 0.20 + 0.70 × 0.05 = 0.095, so 9.5% of all incidents should be flagged and routed. These reports concern rights in medical settings and therefore fit the health-related legal-complaint queue. Classifying an allegation for review does not establish its truth or prove malpractice.

distractor_analysis.reason: It correctly identifies the scheduling remedy and routing rate but accepts II, overlooking that debridement-only consent and express refusal prohibit the stipulated nonemergency amputation.

It lists correct facts from the participating domains but does not integrate them into the requested audit: it neither selects III and its circular-wait target nor applies the computed rate to queue routing.

It incorrectly makes protection of patient rights a justification for simultaneous use of an indivisible exclusive resource. Consent protection does not remove the mutual-exclusion requirement; III instead addresses circular wait.

question: In an emergency decision-support simulator, a hardware interrupt announces each case; a separate application recommends a response. The benchmark has two mutually exclusive, exhaustive classes: • 60%: unconscious patients with BP 70/35 mmHg and HR 42/min, already given oxygen. The application recommends immediate transcutaneous pacing (epinephrine or dopamine if pacing is unavailable) in 90% of these cases and five-minute observation otherwise. • 40%: massive paracetamol overdoses. The application recommends intravenous N-acetylcysteine in 80% of these cases and intravenous glutathione otherwise. Which complete validation trace correctly identifies the interrupt handler's software membership, the appropriate routes according to the clinical cases, and the overall probability of an appropriate recommendation with its probability law? This probability measures benchmark recommendation accuracy, not patient survival.

options.A: OS handler; pacing with the stated fallback, and either overdose route; 94% accuracy by the law of total probability.
options.B: OS handler; pacing with the stated fallback, and intravenous N-acetylcysteine only; 86% accuracy by the law of total probability.
options.C: OS handler; pacing with the stated fallback, and intravenous N-acetylcysteine only; the law of total probability applies, but overall accuracy is not calculated.
options.D: OS handler; pacing with the stated fallback, and intravenous N-acetylcysteine only; 72% accuracy by multiplying the two classes' conditional accuracies.

explanation: The interrupt-handling program belongs to operating system software, distinct from the stipulated recommendation application. The unstable bradycardia case calls for immediate transcutaneous pacing, with epinephrine or dopamine if pacing is unavailable, rather than observation. For massive paracetamol overdose, the supplied case selects intravenous N-acetylcysteine to protect against fatal liver necrosis, not intravenous glutathione. Thus the class-specific probabilities of an appropriate recommendation are 0.90 and 0.80. Because the classes partition the benchmark, the law of total probability gives P(appropriate) = 0.60 × 0.90 + 0.40 × 0.80 = 0.86, or 86%. This is recommendation accuracy, not a survival probability.

distractor_analysis.reason: It incorrectly counts intravenous glutathione as an appropriate overdose response. This inflates the overdose class's accuracy to 100% and produces 0.60 × 0.90 + 0.40 × 1 = 94%.

It lists the correct software membership, treatments, and probability law separately, but does not connect the appropriate routes to their conditional probabilities and calculate the requested overall accuracy.

It multiplies 0.90 by 0.80 as though correct recommendations in both classes must occur together. Each case belongs to exactly one class, so the conditional accuracies must instead be weighted by class frequencies and summed.

question: In an emergency decision-support simulator, a hardware interrupt announces each case, and a separate application recommends a response. The benchmark has two mutually exclusive, exhaustive classes: • 60%: unconscious patients with BP 70/35 mmHg and HR 42/min, already given oxygen. The application recommends immediate transcutaneous pacing (epinephrine or dopamine if pacing is unavailable) 90% of the time and five-minute observation otherwise. • 40%: massive paracetamol overdoses. The application recommends intravenous N-acetylcysteine 80% of the time and intravenous glutathione otherwise. Which validation trace correctly identifies the interrupt handler's software membership, the appropriate response routes, and the overall recommendation accuracy with its probability law? Accuracy here measures benchmark recommendations, not patient survival.

options.A: OS software; pacing with the stated fallback, and either overdose route; law of total probability: 0.60 × 0.90 + 0.40 × 1 = 94%.
options.B: OS software; pacing with the stated fallback, and IV N-acetylcysteine; law of total probability: 0.60 × 0.90 + 0.40 × 0.80 = 86%.
options.C: OS software; pacing with the stated fallback, and IV N-acetylcysteine; law of total probability applies, but overall accuracy is left uncalculated.
options.D: OS software; pacing with the stated fallback, and IV N-acetylcysteine; multiplication rule for independent events: 0.90 × 0.80 = 72%.

explanation: The interrupt-handling program belongs to operating system software, distinct from the stipulated recommendation application. For the unconscious, severely hypotensive patient with bradycardia, the supplied clinical case selects immediate transcutaneous pacing, with epinephrine or dopamine if pacing is unavailable, rather than observation. For massive paracetamol overdose, the supplied chemistry case selects intravenous N-acetylcysteine to protect against fatal liver necrosis, not intravenous glutathione. Thus, the conditional probabilities of an appropriate recommendation are 0.90 and 0.80. Because the classes partition the benchmark, the law of total probability gives P(appropriate) = 0.60 × 0.90 + 0.40 × 0.80 = 0.86. This is recommendation accuracy, not a survival probability.

distractor_analysis.reason: It incorrectly counts intravenous glutathione as an appropriate overdose countermeasure. The supplied case selects only intravenous N-acetylcysteine, so the overdose class contributes 0.40 × 0.80, not 0.40 × 1.
It lists the correct software membership, treatments, and probability law but does not connect the appropriate routes to their conditional probabilities and calculate the requested overall accuracy.

It treats the two class-specific accuracies as independent events that must occur together. Each case belongs to only one class, so their conditional accuracies must be weighted by class frequency and summed, not multiplied.

question: An emergency decision-support simulator receives each case through a hardware interrupt; a separate application recommends a response. Its benchmark has two mutually exclusive, exhaustive classes: • 60%: unconscious patients with BP 70/35 mmHg and HR 42/min, already given oxygen. The application recommends immediate transcutaneous pacing (epinephrine or dopamine if pacing is unavailable) in 90% of cases and five-minute observation otherwise. • 40%: massive paracetamol overdoses. The application recommends intravenous N-acetylcysteine in 80% of cases and intravenous glutathione otherwise. Which validation trace correctly identifies the interrupt handler's software membership, the appropriate response routes, and the overall probability of an appropriate recommendation with its governing probability law? Evaluate benchmark recommendation accuracy, not patient survival.

options.A: OS software; pacing with the stated fallback, and either overdose route; overall accuracy 94%, by the law of total probability.
options.B: OS software; pacing with the stated fallback, and IV N-acetylcysteine only; overall accuracy 86%, by the law of total probability.
options.C: OS software; pacing with the stated fallback, and IV N-acetylcysteine only; law of total probability; class accuracies 90% and 80%, with no overall result.
options.D: OS software; pacing with the stated fallback, and IV N-acetylcysteine only; overall accuracy 72%, by the multiplication rule for independent events.

explanation: The interrupt-handling program belongs to operating system software, distinct from the stipulated recommendation application. The supplied clinical case supports immediate transcutaneous pacing, with epinephrine or dopamine if pacing is unavailable, rather than observation for the unconscious, severely hypotensive patient with bradycardia. The overdose sample selects IV N-acetylcysteine to protect against fatal liver necrosis, not IV glutathione. Thus the conditional probabilities of an appropriate recommendation are 0.90 and 0.80. Because the two classes partition the benchmark, the law of total probability gives P(appropriate) = 0.60 × 0.90 + 0.40 × 0.80 = 0.86. This is recommendation accuracy, not a probability of survival.

distractor_analysis.reason: It incorrectly counts IV glutathione as appropriate alongside IV N-acetylcysteine. This makes the overdose class appear 100% accurate and inflates the weighted result to 0.60 × 0.90 + 0.40 × 1 = 94%.

It states the correct software classification, treatments, probability law, and class accuracies separately, but never combines them using the class frequencies. It therefore fails to supply the requested overall benchmark accuracy.

It multiplies 0.90 by 0.80 as though success in both classes were a required joint event. Each case belongs to exactly one class, so the conditional accuracies must instead be weighted by 0.60 and 0.40 and summed.

retrieval.query_instruction: Given a knowledge requirement, retrieve question-answer samples that provide the domain concepts, mechanisms, rules, or methods needed to satisfy it.

question: A clinical-nutrition service evaluates a 17-year-old girl who has lost 10 kg in six months and has thirst and frequent urination; BP is 100/70 mmHg, with no other notable findings. It can initially arrange only one diagnostic test. It also uses liquid chromatography to analyze multiple different sugars in a dietary beverage. Workflow vertices are T (perform the chosen diagnostic test), D (select the detector), L (perform the sugar assay), R (assemble a report containing both results and HealthKit weight data), U (obtain user authorization), and S (share the report with an external coaching agency). Required edges are D→L, T→R, L→R, and R→S. The applicable policy states: “We will never share with or sell the information gained through the use of Apple HealthKit, such as age, weight and heart rate data, to advertisers or other agencies without your authorization.” Add the policy-required edge, but do not make authorization a prerequisite for testing. There is no direct edge between D and S. Which option selects the appropriate test and detector, gives a valid topological order, and correctly assesses whether S could precede D?

options.A: Fingertip blood glucose; RI detector. Order: T, D, L, R, S; U is optional. S cannot precede D.
options.B: Fingertip blood glucose; RI detector. Add U→S. Order: T, D, L, R, U, S. S cannot precede D.
options.C: Fingertip blood glucose is appropriate; RI is suitable for sugars; HealthKit disclosure requires authorization; topological orders prohibit paths from later to earlier vertices.
options.D: Fingertip blood glucose; RI detector. Add U→S. Order: T, U, R, S, D, L. S may precede D because no direct edge connects them.

explanation: The medical vignette supports fingertip blood glucose as the initial test, and the chromatography sample identifies an RI detector for multiple sugars. Because the report includes HealthKit weight data and is sent to an external agency, the policy adds U→S, not an authorization prerequisite for testing. In B, every prerequisite precedes its dependent vertex. Although D→S is not a direct edge, D→L→R→S is a directed path. Placing S before D would therefore create a path from a later vertex to an earlier one, which is impossible in a topological ordering.

distractor_analysis.reason: It preserves the testing and reporting dependencies but treats authorization as optional, omitting the policy-required U→S dependency before external disclosure of HealthKit weight data.
Its individual facts are correct, but it does not integrate them into the requested prerequisite graph, provide a workflow order, or assess the specific D-to-S relationship.
It incorrectly treats the absence of a direct edge as permission to reverse an indirect dependency. The path D→L→R→S requires D before S; the proposed order also places R before its prerequisite L.

question_plan: Create a hypothetical bond-dispute screening task whose contract contains the supplied one-year filing clause, stipulated to govern the screening without requiring an enforceability analysis. A newest-first singly linked list contains: claim B filed March 1, 2025; claim A filed January 15, 2025; both claims arose February 1, 2024 when their bonds' yields rose from 8% to 10%; and both bonds were initially valued January 1, 2024. Each bond initially costs 800 yuan, has modified duration 10 years, and pays a 6% annual coupon. Stipulate that each claimant requests the duration-estimated price loss, without implying legal entitlement to compensation. Ask how the Inverse algorithm reconstructs chronological order, which claim passes the contractual timing screen, and what fraction and decimal of the combined initial bond value its claimed loss represents.

answer_plans.plan: Repeatedly remove the original list's head node and insert it at the head of a new list. The result orders initial valuations, claim accrual, A's filing, then B's filing. Estimate each price change as -10 × 800 × (0.10 - 0.08) = -160 yuan. Measure the one-year filing period from February 1, 2024: A is timely and B is permanently barred under the stipulated clause. The timely claimed loss is 160 yuan, representing 160/1600 = 1/10 = 0.10 of the combined initial value. This is timing screening, not a finding of liability.

Reverse the linked list correctly and calculate each 160-yuan estimated loss, but omit the filing-deadline screen. Count both claims and report 320 yuan, or 320/1600 = 1/5 = 0.20 of the combined initial value.

Explain head-insertion reversal, calculate the two bond losses, correctly identify A as timely and B as barred, and explain fractions as division. However, leave these results disconnected by reporting the unfiltered combined loss fraction 320/1600 instead of using the legal screening result to select the numerator.

Reverse the list and calculate the losses correctly, but incorrectly treat the first chronological valuation node as the start of the contractual filing period. Measuring from January 1, 2024 rather than the stated February 1 claim-accrual date incorrectly bars both claims and produces a timely-loss fraction of zero.

financial.necessity: Connect the yield increase to the estimated bond-price decrease.
Use 0.02 as the yield change rather than confusing the coupon rate with the yield movement.
Supply the estimated loss attached to each claim before contractual timing screening.

legal.necessity: Start the filing clock at the stated claim-accrual event, not the earlier valuation event.
Determine from the reconstructed chronology whether each claim was filed within the contractual period.
Exclude claim B's requested amount from the timely-claim total under the stipulated screening rule.

mathematics.necessity: Interpret the requested loss fraction as timely claimed loss divided by combined initial value.
Keep 160 yuan as the dividend and 1600 yuan as the divisor rather than reversing their relationship.
Evaluate 160/1600 as 1/10 and 0.10 for the requested final outputs.

question: A bond-dispute system stores events in a newest-first singly linked list: B filed March 1, 2025 → A filed January 15, 2025 → both claims arose February 1, 2024 → both bonds were initially valued January 1, 2024. Each bond initially cost 800 yuan, had modified duration 10 years, and paid a 6% annual coupon. Both claims arose when yields increased from 8% to 10%; each claimant requests the duration-estimated price loss. The contract states that any dispute must be filed within one year after the claim arose; otherwise it is permanently barred. Apply this clause as stipulated, without assessing enforceability or liability. Which option correctly describes Inverse reconstruction into chronological order, identifies timely claims, and gives their total requested loss as a fraction and decimal of the combined initial bond value?

options.A: Remove each original head and insert it at the new head: valuation → accrual → A → B. Count both claims without a deadline screen: 320 yuan; 1/5 = 0.20.
options.B: Remove each original head and insert it at the new head: valuation → accrual → A → B. Only A passes; B is barred: 160 yuan; 1/10 = 0.10.
options.C: Remove each original head and insert it at the new head: valuation → accrual → A → B. Only A passes; B is barred. Report both claims' combined loss: 320 yuan; 1/5 = 0.20.
options.D: Remove each original head and insert it at the new head: valuation → accrual → A → B. Start the filing period at valuation; both claims are barred: 0 yuan; 0/1600 = 0.00.

explanation: Repeatedly removing the original head and inserting it at the new list's head reverses the event order. Modified duration gives each bond's estimated price change as −10 × 800 × (0.10 − 0.08) = −160 yuan. The contractual filing period begins at claim accrual on February 1, 2024, not at initial valuation. A's January 15, 2025 filing is timely; B's March 1, 2025 filing is permanently barred under the stipulated clause. Thus the timely requested loss is 160 yuan. A fraction expresses division, so its share of the combined initial value is 160/1600 = 1/10 = 0.10. Passing this timing screen does not establish liability.

distractor_analysis.reason: It reverses the list and estimates the losses correctly but omits the contractual filing screen, improperly counting B's barred claim.
It correctly states the reversal, timing results, and combined-loss fraction separately, but fails to use the timing result to select only A's loss for the numerator.
It incorrectly treats the first event in chronological order as the legal deadline trigger. The clause starts the period when the claims arose, not when the bonds were initially valued.

question: A hypothetical bond contract states that any dispute must be filed within one year after the claim arose; otherwise it is permanently barred. Apply this clause solely as a timing screen, without assessing enforceability or liability. A newest-first singly linked event list is B → A → R → V: B filed March 1, 2025; A filed January 15, 2025; both claims arose at R on February 1, 2024, when bond yields rose from 8% to 10%; and both bonds were initially valued at V on January 1, 2024. Each bond initially cost 800 yuan, had modified duration 10 years, and paid a 6% annual coupon. Each claimant requests the duration-estimated price loss. Which option gives the Inverse algorithm's reconstruction method and chronological order, the timing-screen result, and the timely claimed loss as a fraction and decimal of the combined initial bond value?

options.A: Repeatedly remove the original head and insert it at the new head; V → R → A → B. Count both claims without a deadline screen: 320/1600 = 1/5 = 0.20.
options.B: Repeatedly remove the original head and insert it at the new head; V → R → A → B. Only A passes: 160/1600 = 1/10 = 0.10.
options.C: Repeatedly remove the original head and insert it at the new head; V → R → A → B. Only A passes, but report both claims' losses: 320/1600 = 1/5 = 0.20.
options.D: Repeatedly remove the original head and insert it at the new head; V → R → A → B. Start the filing clock at V, so neither passes: 0/1600 = 0 = 0.00.

explanation: Removing successive original head nodes and inserting each at the head of an initially empty new list reverses B → A → R → V into V → R → A → B. Modified duration estimates each price change as −10 × 800 × (0.10 − 0.08) = −160 yuan, so each requested loss is 160 yuan. The contractual year runs from claim accrual on February 1, 2024, not initial valuation. A filed within that year; B filed after it and is permanently barred under the stipulated screen. The timely requested amount is therefore 160 yuan. Fractions express division, so its share of the combined initial value is 160/(800 + 800) = 1/10 = 0.10. Passing the timing screen does not establish liability or entitlement to compensation.

It correctly states the reversal, timing result, and division for the combined losses, but fails to connect the timing result to the numerator: only A's 160-yuan loss belongs in the requested fraction.

question: A bond-dispute screening system stores events in a newest-first singly linked list: B → A → E → V. V records both bonds' initial valuations on January 1, 2024; E records both claims arising on February 1, 2024, when yields rose from 8% to 10%; A and B record filings on January 15 and March 1, 2025, respectively. Each bond initially costs 800 yuan, has modified duration 10 years, and pays a 6% annual coupon. Each claimant requests the duration-estimated price loss. The contract states that any dispute must be commenced or filed within one year after the claim arose; otherwise, it is permanently barred. Assume this clause governs screening without an enforceability analysis; passing the screen does not establish liability. Which option correctly gives the Inverse reversal operation and resulting chronology, the claims passing the timing screen, and their total requested loss as a fraction and decimal of the combined initial bond value?

options.A: Repeatedly remove the original head and insert it at the new head: V → E → A → B. Both claims pass; 320/1600 = 1/5 = 0.20.
options.B: Repeatedly remove the original head and insert it at the new head: V → E → A → B. Only A passes; 160/1600 = 1/10 = 0.10.
options.C: Repeatedly remove the original head and insert it at the new head: V → E → A → B. Only A passes, but report both losses: 320/1600 = 1/5 = 0.20.
options.D: Repeatedly remove the original head and insert it at the new head: V → E → A → B. Neither claim passes the January 1, 2025 deadline; 0/1600 = 0 = 0.00.

explanation: Removing successive original heads and inserting each at the head of an initially empty new list reverses B → A → E → V into V → E → A → B. Modified duration gives an estimated price change of −10 × 800 × (0.10 − 0.08) = −160 yuan per bond; the coupon rate is not the yield change. The stipulated filing period begins when the claims arose on February 1, 2024, not at initial valuation. A was filed within one year; B was filed after that period and is permanently barred under the stipulated clause. Thus, the screened requested loss is 160 yuan. Fractions express division, so its share of the combined initial value is 160/(800 + 800) = 1/10 = 0.10. This is a timing result, not a finding of liability.

distractor_analysis.reason: It reverses the list and calculates the losses correctly but omits the contractual deadline, incorrectly counting B as timely.

It correctly identifies the reversal, individual losses, and timing outcome, but fails to connect screening to the numerator. B's excluded loss must not contribute to the requested timely-loss fraction.
It incorrectly uses the first chronological node, initial valuation, as the legal clock's trigger. The clause instead measures one year from claim accrual on February 1, 2024, so A passes.

question_plan: Construct an educational infusion-pump simulation, not a clinical prescription. Using the retrieved dopamine dose-band convention, ask for the midpoint dose associated with beta1 effects in a hypothetical 60 kg patient with hypotensive septic shock. Specify a hypothetical solution containing 0.020% active dopamine by mass with density 1.00 g/mL, and a pump delivering 0.010 mL per pulse. Assume ideal delivery and define the bus message as a control signal encoding pulse frequency. Ask what information the controller receives from the data bus and what frequency in pulses/second that control signal must encode. Require the concentration and unit-conversion calculations.

answer_plans.plan: Identify the received information as a control signal. Use the sample's 5–10 micrograms/kg/min dose band and its midpoint, 7.5 micrograms/kg/min, giving 450 micrograms/min for 60 kg. Convert 0.020% to mass fraction 0.00020; multiplying by 1.00 g/mL gives 0.00020 g/mL, or 200 micrograms/mL. Required delivery is 2.25 mL/min. Divide by 0.010 mL/pulse to obtain 225 pulses/min, then divide by 60 to obtain a control-signal frequency of 3.75 pulses/second.

Incorrectly choose the 1–4 micrograms/kg/min band for the requested beta1 effect and use its midpoint, 2.5. Correctly perform the remaining concentration and rate calculations, producing 1.25 pulses/second rather than 3.75, while identifying the bus information as a control signal.

Correctly state that the controller receives a control signal, identify the 5–10 dose band and its midpoint, calculate the solution concentration, and explain quantity/rate and minute/second conversions separately. Do not combine them into the required pump flow or encoded frequency.

Correctly calculate the patient requirement of 450 micrograms/min and concentration of 200 micrograms/mL, but multiply dose requirement by concentration instead of dividing. Treat the dimensionally invalid result as mL/min and use it to calculate the bus frequency, incorrectly implying that a more concentrated solution requires faster pumping.

medical.necessity: The supplied answer identifies 5–10 micrograms/kg/min as the band whose midpoint the simulation requires.
The micrograms/kg/min units require multiplying the midpoint dose by the hypothetical patient's mass.
This preserves the clinical context in which the retrieved sample asks about dopamine's beta1 effects.

chemistry.necessity: Interpreting the supplied percentage as a mass fraction determines the active-drug mass per unit solution mass.

geography.completion:
Working model Decollement/detachment layer refers to a relatively weak rock-structure combination layer above the underlying rock combination, controlled by the overlying folded rock combination, and characterized by strong shear deformation. Multiple detachment layers may develop simultaneously or continuously during lithosphere deformation, and detachment layers may develop on different structural scales, so multi-layer detachment tectonics is the main mode of lithosphere deformation. The discovery of large-scale low-angle faults, such as extensional detachment faults[1,2] and large-scale low-angle thrust faults[3,4], has led structural geologists to propose that the continental lithosphere may be stratified according to physical properties . Therefore, when the lithosphere undergoes large-scale structural deformation, structural detachment may occur along the physical property mutation interface, forming a lithosphere-scale decollement fault. These detachment faults divide the lithosphere into structural layers with different petrophysical properties. Due to the different depths and temperature-pressure conditions of each structural layer, the deformation behavior of each structural layer is also different. A variety of hypothetical models have been proposed for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere. For example, in the Himalayas, southern Tibet, and other orogenic belts, under the thickening of the lithosphere, it is proposed that the middle-crust channel (or channel) flow model (mid-crustal ductile channel flow) to adjust the excess mass, which explains the phenomenon of the coexistence of surface extension and compression structures[5~7]. Jackson [8]'s continental lithosphere sandwich structure model (Fig. 1) uses the relationship between lithospheric rock physical conditions and temperature and pressure conditions to explain the reasons for the occurrence and existence of delamination structures. Evidence problem
Fig. 1 	Jackson lithosphere sandwich structure model [8] The lithosphere multi-layer detachment structure model has been supported by some field observations and experimental evidence, mainly including: ① Field observation support. Since the deformation traces of the deep structural layers of the lithosphere can be exposed under tectonic action, in some special structural parts, the structural traces formed by different structural layers of the lithosphere during the same tectonic process can "co-exist". A detailed structural analysis of such structural sites, supplemented by analysis of petrology, geochemistry and chronology, can gain new understanding. For example, based on the observation of low-angle normal faults in the North American Cordillera, Wernicke[1] and Lister et al.[2] proposed that low-angle normal faults are ductile shear zones in the middle crust, formed by extensional detachment (Fig. 2), the footwall formed a metamorphic core complex and the hanging wall formed a basin and range structure due to tilting. On the profile, the metamorphic core complex is composed of deep core metamorphic complex, middle-level ductile shear-detachment fault and shallow-level brittle deformation structure, and has the characteristics of three-layer structure. For an in-depth analysis of ductile detachment faults, the type of shear action and its variation can be quantitatively determined by kinematic vorticity, so as to establish a structural kinematic model[7, 9]. In the Hunan-Hubei-Chongqing-Sichuan border area of the middle and upper Yangtze in South China, Yan et al. [10], through the observation and analysis of the relationship between different styles of fault-fold combinations under the condition of thrust and nappe, proposed that the shallow lithosphere structure consists of multiple The thick-skinned-thin-skinned structural model of layered progressive pushover controlled by layer detachment structure (Fig. 3). The above shows that multi-layer detachment tectonics can develop in different structural layers of lithosphere. Fig. 2. 	Three delaminated tectonic models in the formation of low-angle normal faults and metamorphic core complex structures[1,2] Brittle upper crust; 2. Ductile crust; 3. Lithospheric upper mantle; 4. Asthenosphere; 5. Magmatic rock② Evidence from deep geophysical exploration. The most important evidence support for the multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere comes from the results of deep geophysical exploration, including deep seismic reflection, magnetotelluric sounding, and Bouguer gravity anomaly detection. After the 5.12 Longmenshan Wenchuan Earthquake in 2008, Burchfiel et al. [11], based on data such as the Bouguer gravity anomaly, believed that the upper crust of Longmenshan did not thicken significantly, but the middle and lower crust with one to several layers of ductile flow crust was flowing eastward. In the process, it was blocked and thickened by the hard central Sichuan block under the Sichuan Basin, resulting in the vertical uplift of Longmenshan and the accumulation of abnormal stress, which eventually led to the Wenchuan earthquake in May 2008. This indicates that there is a multi-layer detachment structure of the lithosphere in the Longmen Mountains and the area to the west. This structural model of Burchfiel et al. [11] further proves that the passage (or channel) flow mode [5~7]. In many mountain ranges, detachment faults have been recognized as one of the dominant factors of orogeny, such as the use of deep reflection seismic profiling (CORCOP) to discover a huge near-horizontal fault beneath the Blue Ridge of the Appalachians in the United States Thrust detachment zone, and pushed the Precambrian crystalline rock series of the Blue Ridge on the sedimentary cover of the Lower Paleozoic, and the thrust distance from the southeast to the northwest of the 5-15km thick foreign rock sheet Up to 260km[3, 4]. ③ Supported by experimental simulation results. In order to verify the multi-layer detachment structure model of the lithosphere, people use petrological and geochemical analysis methods, or carry out relevant high-temperature, high-pressure and petrological experimental analysis on rock samples at different structural levels, and on this basis put forward The delamination structural model of the lithosphere [12] better explains the deep structural detachment of the lithosphere. Figure 3 	Formation model of multi-layered detached nappe thin-skinned structures in the South China Yangtze block [6] Fz, Fc, Fs and Ft represent the structural detachment of the Sinian base, Cambrian base, Silurian and Triassic lower parts, respectively Some key scientific issues involved in the detachment surface[10] Although the multi-layer detachment structural model of the continental lithosphere has been supported by some observations and experimental evidence, there are still some key scientific issues that have not been resolved. Therefore, the multi-layer detachment structural model It is still a working hypothesis. These scientific issues mainly include: ① How to determine the interface properties of structural layer detachment? That is, what is the underground originality? For example, the physical properties and deformation behavior of the structural layer interface are the most critical issues in the deformation of multi-layer detachment structures. What we have observed in the field is the structural traces of the lithosphere exposed to the surface after multi-layer detachment and deformation. However, the interface inferred from deep geophysical data has multiple solutions. How to compare it with surface observations becomes a solution. the crux of the matter. Some researchers have also proposed to use high temperature and high pressure experiments to test. However, due to the limitation of the strain rate and boundary conditions such as temperature and pressure during the experiment, the current simulation is far from the actual environment of natural deformation. ② What is the deformation process of structural layer detachment? That is, what kind of deformation and metamorphism process has it experienced? When we observe on the surface, we invert the deformation process according to some structural kinematics pointing signs during the deformation. However, during the observation process, it was also found that many kinematic directions at the same time were inconsistent or even opposite. In addition, the deformation process we are inverting now does not limit the time and deformation rate, and even completely ignores the deformation process. Therefore, this inversion process may be very different from the natural process. ③ Reasons for deformation differences between structural layers? Among the different structural layers observed in the field, there are huge differences in deformation structural styles and combinations, as well as the metamorphic temperature-pressure conditions reflected by them, but the interface between the two layers, that is, the ductile detachment shear zone, may sometimes only be a few centimeters. What is the reason, what is the tectonic process, and the tectonic force can cause such a huge deformation-metamorphism difference between the upper and lower structural layers? ④ How big is the scale of delamination? Since the multi-layer detachment is based on the observation of low-angle faults, the change and extension scale/depth of low-angle faults are the most important basis for determining the scale of delamination. However, there is no research example so far that can accurately determine The occurrence change and scale of low-angle faults to the deep. Another question related to this is whether this kind of delamination structure only occurs in the middle and upper part of the lithosphere, or can it occur in the entire continental lithosphere? For example, is the delamination at the bottom of the lithosphere[12] a type of delamination tectonics? ⑤ Is there really a middle and lower crustal ductile channel flow in the middle and lower crust? Is it one layer or several layers? Is the multilayer detachment tectonics of the lithosphere controlled by the flow of these ductile flow shells? Or to what extent can the ductile flow crust control the deformation of the lithosphere? How to determine the nature of this fluid? There are no definitive answers to questions about the relative viscosities or rheology of fluids. Since the above key problems have not been resolved, traditional structural geology field observations are limited by surface rock outcrops, there are uncertainties and multi-solutions in the interpretation of deep geophysical detection data, and rock geochemical data have limitations in geological relationship analysis. Insufficient, especially the boundary conditions set by experimental structural geology are far from satisfying the physical, chemical and geological reality of the deep deformation of the continental lithosphere. Therefore, only by combining the studies of structural geology, geophysics and rock geochemistry, and realizing the complementary advantages of multiple disciplines, can objectively carry out more in-depth research on the multi-layer delamination structure of the lithosphere. With the continuous refinement of field structural analysis and the discovery of new important evidence and key structural phenomena, coupled with the continuous application of modern testing and simulation techniques in the field of earth sciences, the temperature-pressure conditions at different depths of the lithosphere and their Morphing features will gradually become a reality. On the basis of these studies, the continental lithosphere multi-layer delamination model will be continuously revised and improved.

question:
coronal heating mechanism
answer:
geography.completion: On July 22, 2009, residents in the middle and lower reaches of the Yangtze River in my country witnessed a total solar eclipse once in hundreds of years. This is the most spectacular total solar eclipse in the 21st century. Many, it is rare. In fact, as early as 2,000 years ago, there were records of solar eclipse observations in ancient China. When a total solar eclipse occurs, we can see the weak scattered light radiated from the outer atmosphere of the sun to the photosphere. These scattered lights have a coronal structure, so the outer atmosphere is called the corona (Figure 1). The first successful photocoronagraphy was taken during a solar eclipse in 1851. In 1931, he began to use a coronagraph to observe the corona when there is no solar eclipse. Coronal hyperthermia was first observed by sounding rockets in 1946. Since the 1970s, high-resolution instruments have been used to observe the corona on the ground and satellites, such as Skylab, and use soft and hard X-rays to study the activities of the corona, opening up a new era of exploring the corona[1]. Figure 1 The corona of the sun photographed during a total solar eclipse The sun is a hot gas ball, which can be divided into four layers: the nuclear reaction zone, the radiation layer, the troposphere and the solar atmosphere from the center to the edge of the sun. The solar atmosphere is the outermost and only visible layer of the sun. The temperature, density, and magnetic field in the solar atmosphere vary greatly. People often divide the solar atmosphere into the photosphere, chromosphere, transition layer, and corona according to the change of temperature with altitude (Figure 2). The corona is the outermost layer of the solar atmosphere, which is composed of a very thin and fully ionized high-temperature plasma, mainly protons, highly ionized ions and high-speed free electrons [1]. As early as the first half of the 19th century, the emission lines Fe X and XIV in the corona were discovered, which can only occur when the temperature of the corona is as high as one million degrees. The temperature in the central nuclear reaction zone of the sun is as high as 15 million ℃, and the temperature decreases rapidly from the center to the outside, and the temperature on the surface of the sun (photosphere, chromosphere) is only about 6000 ℃. And when it reaches the corona of the outer atmosphere of the sun, the temperature not only does not drop but rises by two orders of magnitude to millions of degrees (Figure 2), which is contrary to the natural law that heat can only be directed from high temperature areas to low temperature areas. There must be some kind of heating mechanism that can balance the energy loss (mainly convective radiation and solar wind loss) caused by various dissipation mechanisms in the corona to maintain such a high temperature in the corona. The mechanism of coronal heating, one of the most challenging problems in solar physics, has puzzled many scientists for many years. Figure 2 	The solar atmosphere is divided into photosphere, chromosphere, transition zone and corona. 500km down from the temperature pole is the photosphere, while the height H of the chromosphere is from 200 to 2200km, and its bottom is located in the temperature pole. The thickness of the low chromosphere is about 400km, and the temperature begins to rise; the range of the middle chromosphere is about 1200km, and the temperature rises slowly from 5500K to 8500K; the thickness of the high chromosphere is about 500km, and the temperature rises rapidly to 50 000K. The base of the corona is about at H=3000km. The area from the top of the chromosphere to the bottom of the corona is the transition zone, and the temperature rises sharply from tens of thousands of kelvins to 106K[2] Many different theoretical mechanisms have been proposed in the research on the problem of coronal heating, and it is believed that the convective movement of the plasma below the photosphere Drive the movement of the coronal loop magnetic field lines rooted in the photosphere (the root point is the foot point, Figure 3 is the image of the coronal loop), causing changes in the topological configuration of the magnetic field, accumulating magnetic energy, and then converting it into heat energy by a certain mechanism to heat the coronal plasma body. The mechanical motion of the photosphere and the matter inside it is the ultimate source of coronal heating energy. Based on the comparison of the characteristic time scale of coronal loop foot point motion rooted in the photosphere and the characteristic time of local shear Alfvén wave propagation, the coronal heating mechanism can be roughly divided into: DC heating and AC heating Heating) two categories. DC heating, also known as ohmic heating, such as current sheet heating in simple Joule heating and magnetic reconnection process, etc., this kind of heating foot point movement is slow; AC heating is caused by plasma wave-particle interaction, such as acoustic heating , fast and slow magnetic acoustic wave heating, Alfven wave heating and ion cyclotron resonance heating, etc., the foot point moves faster during the AC heating process. Ohmic heating theory is the process of magnetic energy passing through classic ohmic heating and current dissipation, and the movement of the foot point is relatively slow. Because the resistivity in the corona is very small, it is obvious that heating by ohms is not enough for the coronal temperature Fig. 3 	coronal loop image [3]. This requires the appearance of a small-scale structure, in which there is a large magnetic field gradient, so that a large current density can be generated, and the dissipation of magnetic energy can be accelerated through ohmic heating, so that the coronal temperature requirement can be met. In fact, the convective movement of the feet of the magnetic force lines in the corona can indeed promote the formation of small-scale current structures, such as small-scale current sheets. In these small-scale current sheets, the magnetofreezing effect in ideal magnetohydrodynamics no longer holds true, and the convergence and reconnection of magnetic force lines generate an electric field and a singular current layer parallel to the magnetic field. In this way, the energy stored in the lines of magnetic force is released in the form of ohmic heating in this strange current layer. The corresponding heating mechanism has been studied by a lot of work [4-9]. However, the conversion process of magnetic energy to thermal energy is still a great challenge before us. AC heating, also known as wave heating theory, believes that the movement of foot points excites various modes of waves in the coronal plasma, and the wave energy is dissipated into plasma energy to heat the corona through the form of wave-particle interaction. Foot movement can generate a series of wide-spectrum fluctuations, such as sound waves, Alfven waves, and fast and slow magnetoacoustic waves. Acoustic waves and slow waves will form shock waves during their upward propagation, and it is difficult to pass into the corona due to strong dissipation; while the refraction and reflection of fast waves are very serious. Alfven waves are most likely to enter the coronal plasma, and it is indeed found that there are Alfven waves in the corona in the observations. Because the Alfvén wave is a transverse wave, the shock wave will not be formed during the propagation process, and the energy of the wave will propagate along the magnetic force line. However, due to its weak damping properties, it is difficult to dissipate energy in the coronal plasma and cannot provide sufficient heating power for the corona. Generally speaking, due to the lack of understanding of coronal fluctuations (type, energy flow, wave spectrum), we still cannot well understand the AC heating mechanism of the corona[10]. Although there are various other theoretical mechanisms, the common point is that coronal heating is caused by the convective motion of plasma on the surface of the sun, and the twisting of the coronal magnetic field lines at the feet of the photosphere drives the change of the topological configuration of the coronal loop magnetic field caused by. Therefore, the observation of the solar magnetic field and the analysis of these observation data and the comparison with the existing theoretical models are the key to the study of the coronal heating mechanism. Due to the limitations of the existing observation conditions, it is difficult for us to judge which heating mechanism plays a decisive role in the process of coronal heating. Fortunately, the Hinode (Sunrise, 2006—) satellite, which aims to determine the solar coronal heating mechanism as one of its scientific goals, has been launched, and the Solar Probe Plus (Sun Probe) program is also in the making, which will provide a basis for solving the mystery of coronal heating. Unprecedented opportunity.
